message.content: The color of the sea can vary depending on several factors, but it is most commonly described as blue. This blue hue comes from the way water absorbs and scatters sunlight. Water absorbs colors at the red end of the spectrum more strongly than those at the blue end, so the blue wavelengths are reflected back to our eyes. Additionally, the presence of algae, plankton, and suspended particles can shift the sea’s appearance toward green or even brownish tones in certain conditions. So while “blue” is the classic description, the sea’s color can range from deep indigo to turquoise, green, or even grayish depending on depth, clarity, and surrounding environment.
